title: RULES for the 24-Hour Grocery Store After Midnight #shorts
description_hook: You stop for milk after midnight. The store is open, the music is on, and the only other sound is the freezers.

lines.say: You stop for milk after midnight. Rule one: if the intercom plays a song you've never heard, keep shopping. Don't hum along.
lines.img: a huge brightly lit suburban grocery store at night seen from the entrance, long empty aisles under fluorescent tubes, polished floor reflecting the light

lines.say: Rule two. Skip any aisle where the lights are off.
lines.img: one grocery aisle sunk in darkness between two fully lit aisles, shelves fading into shadow, an abandoned shopping cart at its mouth

lines.say: Rule three. When a freezer door fogs up, someone is standing behind you. Don't wipe it.
lines.img: close-up of a glass freezer door clouded with fog in a quiet supermarket, cold blue light inside, a vague dark shape blurred in the reflection

lines.say: Rule four. Never use the self-checkout that is already beeping.
lines.img: a row of unattended self-checkout machines at night, one screen glowing brighter than the rest, empty bagging area, harsh overhead light

lines.text: PAY A CASHIER YOU SAW WALK IN
lines.say: Rule five. Only pay a cashier you saw walk in.
lines.img: a single staffed checkout lane seen from far away, a cashier silhouette from behind under a lone lamp, the dark empty parking lot beyond the glass doors

lines.say: Last rule: check your receipt. The milk is already on it. Rung up before you walked in.
lines.img: a long curled paper receipt lying on a checkout belt beside a carton of milk, cold fluorescent light, empty store blurred behind

loop_back: The receipt says you were already rung up before you arrived, so the cashier saw someone walk in before you — rule five bends, and the viewer is sent back to the doors and rule one.

gumi.say: So. Who rang up your milk?
